parsed.notes:
Several judgment calls in this posting are flagged for review.
Responsibilities name Spanner Graph, Vertex AI Pipelines, MLflow, feature stores and APIs. None of these is asked of the candidate in a qualifications section, so they are not labeled.
The 8+ years line ('machine learning, data, or software engineering') is read as X, Y, or Z alternatives, giving group 1. 'Data engineering' has no taxonomy id.
Machine-learning is flagged uncertain because it could be argued to be asked on its own elsewhere ('deploying ML', 'classical predictive modeling'). I kept it in group 1.
Group 2 is 'knowledge graphs, semantic data models, or entity-resolution systems'. Entity resolution is unmapped, so the group holds only knowledge-graphs and data-modeling.
The knowledge-graphs mention in the preferred list ('publications ... in knowledge graphs') is optional. The required mention wins.
Cloud line: 'cloud' is the broad skill and stays out of group 4. gcp is nice_to_have because of the inline 'preferred' marker. aws and azure are 'acceptable' options under a required item, so they stay required. All three form one alternative group.
'ML frameworks' has no fitting taxonomy id and is not labeled. Only PyTorch, TensorFlow and scikit-learn are labeled.
embeddings comes from 'graph embeddings' (required). Embedding-based matching is also named as an entity-resolution example.
structured-data-extraction is mapped from 'LLM-based information extraction from documents'. Flagged because it is a loose fit.
ai-deployment is mapped from 'Experience deploying ML on a major cloud'. Flagged.
rag is mapped from GraphRAG, a RAG variant, at nice_to_have. Flagged.
nlp is taken from the 'publications, patents or open-source contributions in ... NLP' item. Flagged because it asks for publications rather than skill use.
Model registry is left unmapped rather than forced onto model-versioning or mlflow.
Google ADK and LangGraph are examples of one ask ('agent frameworks (e.g., ...)'), so they form group 5. agents is the named broad skill and stays out of the group.
Degree: a bachelor's is required ('Bachelor’s degree ... or equivalent applicable experience'). Master's/PhD appears under Preferred.
Per 'highest level named' I labeled phd/nice_to_have with or_equivalent false. Alternative reading: bachelor/required/or_equivalent true. Flagged for review.
Seniority is stated by the 'Lead' title. It is also consistent with 8+ years and the mentoring duty.
No German or language requirement appears in the posting.
